data.body:
Operator asked 2026-10-24. START AFTER the 2026-10-24 restart (D-restart-window-2026-10-24: no new agents before). Brief for the research agent: (1) Landscape, primary sources, VERIFIED/REPORTED/UNKNOWN: Kimi K2.x Agent Swarm (what it is, how subagents are spawned and coordinated, limits), Claude Code subagents/agent teams and Agent SDK orchestration patterns, OpenAI Agents SDK handoffs, Codex multi-agent, Cursor background agents and parallel agents, Devin/Cognition multi-Devin, OpenHands, Google ADK/A2A (agent-to-agent protocol), MCP-based coordination, LangGraph/CrewAI/AutoGen patterns, Paseo and other control planes (D-control-planes), Gas Town/Mad-Max style fleets, git-worktree-per-agent practice, Anthropic's multi-agent research system write-up (orchestrator-worker, token costs), Cognition 'don't build multi-agents' critique (context sharing). (2) Algorithms and policies: task decomposition and the dependency graph (ddflow already has needs/globs/waves), work-stealing vs central dispatch, contract-net/auction by capability and cost, bin-packing by file globs to avoid conflicts, critical-path-first scheduling, speculative execution and redundancy for hard items, hedged requests across families, reviewer assignment with independence constraint, backpressure and the load-based parallelism cap (schedule.parallel), fairness queues (the FIFO suite lock), heartbeat/lease failure detection and re-assignment, idempotent resume, straggler handling, budget- and limit-aware routing (TE-limit-aware-routing), quality-aware routing (per model per task kind success rates from gate outcomes), cost/latency models. (3) Data and session sharing: what an agent needs (brief, decisions governing its globs, lessons, memories, the event log, summaries: CC-store, resume pack), shared blackboard = ddflow records vs message passing, what NOT to share (secrets, transcripts: redaction), on-demand transfer (D-session-context), cross-family session continuity, remote agents (network transport, auth, no shared filesystem: bundle/seed-extract, patch/branch handoff, ddflow serve), consistency model of the event log across hosts (merge=union shards, lamport clocks already used). (4) What ddflow has and plans (map ids): launcher, lanes, ACP (D-acp-r2), Paseo (D-control-planes), DRV-lane-interface/engines/model-catalog/plugin-sdk, DSH-lane, TE-limit-aware-routing/TE-auto-resume, P-batch-gates, P-remote-approvals, P-operator-digest, DX-fleet-registry, DX-drain-mode, DX-mixed-fleet-research (merge or link), P-agent-memory, P-orphan-recovery, session-context, ddflow serve/remote tasks (P-remote.*), SE-ask. (5) Proposal: architecture (orchestrator role split: lead vs scheduler daemon vs workers), the scheduling algorithm in layers (hard constraints: globs/needs/independence/budget; scores: critical path, capability fit, cost, queue length), the worker contract (Lane interface), session/data sharing design, remote worker design and trust model, failure and recovery, observability in the operator digest, the pilot (3 local lanes of 3 families on a toy phase, then 1 remote), metrics to prove it is better (throughput, rework, cost per merged item), options A/B/C with a recommendation, what would invalidate it, tasks (SW- prefix) with needs/waves/globs, questions with defaults. Write docs/ddflow/research/swarm-orchestration.md and decisions/swarm-orchestration.md (proposal state).

Folded DX-mixed-fleet-research (Research: a mixed fleet: a Claude lead orchestrating lane workers on other agents and models (opencode+deepseek, kilo+qwen, gemini, grok, cursor, dsh): launch, observe, steer, independence, cost, quality, limits): Its questions and the hook addendum are answered in docs/ddflow/research/swarm-orchestration.md section 8; build work is phase P-swarm.

Operator asked 2026-10-24. Start AFTER the 2026-10-24 restart (decision D-restart-window-2026-10-24: no new agents before). Read first: D-agent-parity (launching with consent), D-acp-r2 (ACP client as lane driver), D-control-planes (Paseo), services/launcher.py, ddflow lanes, D-driver-architecture (Lane interface, DRV-lane-interface, DRV-engines), agent-token-features research (headless/resume/limit per agent), DSH-lane, TE-limit-aware-routing, TE-auto-resume, LS-worker-mcp-config and lean agents. Questions: which agents can run headless or ACP/SDK with the ddflow MCP server at lean-core tier; tool-calling quality of non-Claude models on ddflow's tools (MTD-accuracy-eval: families cost Kimi 31 points on first call: measure flat/core per model); how the Claude lead supervises (lane events, usage ingestion, nudges, resume); lease enforcement where the agent has no hooks (git hooks only); reviewer independence gets easier with mixed fleets; permission/sandbox modes headless; per-lane cost and limit routing; failure modes (a worker model that cannot follow the rules); a pilot design: one lane per agent on a toy item with a conformance run; what ddflow must still build.

ADDED 2026-10-24 (operator question on hooks): for each lane agent decide how hooks are installed: lane-private hook config inside the lane directory (ATF-Q2) versus project files written by ddflow adopt; per-agent hook strength (session start / prompt inject only vs blocking pre-tool hooks for lease enforcement; git commit hook as the fallback); Kimi hooks are in a user file ([REDACTED:path]) so a lane needs its own config dir; Grok has no descriptor hook entry yet; dsh bridge is experimental and fails silently on a bad path; hook identity: hooks must carry the lane's own agent identity (see the identity bug); plugin-style hooks (Kilo/OpenCode) need operator consent and a diff.
